record.context_brief: Stellar properties controlling Type Ia explosions
record.original_question: Among possible Type Ia supernova progenitors with initial masses about 3–8 solar masses, which stellar properties—especially high rotational velocities and magnetic fields in B-type main-sequence stars—can determine whether a star ends by exploding as a Type Ia supernova, with or without a companion?

evidence.quote: As mentioned before, it is most reasonable that SNIa progenitors are stars in the approximate range of 3-8 M⊙, i.e. stars that on the Main Sequence belong to spectral types B.
Many of these stars are known to display high rotational velocities, and may be expected to have high magnetic fields as a result of intense dynamo activity.
Perhaps some of these properties may be THE cause for a given B-type star to end its evolution exploding as a SNIa, whether with or without the help of a companion.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider single stars on the main sequence with initial masses in the approximate range 3–8 solar masses, corresponding to spectral type B. Such stars are observed to display, in many cases, high rotational velocities and are expected, through intense dynamo activity, to develop strong magnetic fields. Identify which intrinsic stellar properties of these B-type main-sequence stars — in particular their rotational velocity distribution and magnetic-field strength and topology — determine whether a given star ultimately ends its evolution as a Type Ia supernova, either as an isolated star or with the assistance of a binary companion. Specify the quantitative criteria on rotation, magnetic field, mass, and (where relevant) companion properties that distinguish those stars whose endpoint is a Type Ia supernova explosion from those whose endpoint is not.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews (2024–2025) describe Type Ia supernova progenitors as a "long-standing puzzle" still unresolved, with competing single-degenerate and double-degenerate channels and no consensus on which intrinsic properties of intermediate-mass B-type progenitors (rotation, magnetic fields) determine the explosion outcome.

status_evidence.title: Type Ia supernova progenitors: a contemporary view of a long-standing puzzle
status_evidence.snippet: Contemporary review describing the progenitor problem as a long-standing, still-open puzzle.
status_evidence.claim: The identification of Type Ia supernova progenitors remains an open problem as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: Type Ia supernovae (arXiv:2411.09740)
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 review discussing competing progenitor channels without a definitive resolution.
status_evidence.claim: No consensus exists on which stellar properties determine SNIa outcomes.
